<reason>Side A won a competitive debate by making the motion easier to decide: a hard floor on basic entry, with parking, events, and concessions as exceptions, plus a ratchet if managers depend on fences. Side B’s scarcity, underfunding, and “enclosure by ruin” case stayed live, especially overflow onto the last free surface, but waivers and off-peak freedom undercut the claim that growing paid gates are required stewardship rather than the enclosure the motion resists.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal that B had only defended already-conceded tools, later met by B’s overflow argument that a no-gate floor wrecks the remaining free lawn.</best_rebuttal>
